objectives.text: The Discount Window plays an important role in supporting the liquidity and stability of the banking system and the effective implementation of monetary policy.

citations.quote: The Discount Window plays an important role in supporting the liquidity and stability of the banking system and the effective implementation of monetary policy.

objectives.text: By providing ready access to funding, the Discount Window helps depository institutions manage their liquidity risks efficiently and avoid actions that have negative consequences for their customers, such as withdrawing credit during times of market stress.

citations.quote: By providing ready access to funding, the Discount Window helps depository institutions manage their liquidity risks efficiently and avoid actions that have negative consequences for their customers, such as withdrawing credit during times of market stress.

objectives.text: Thus, the Discount Window supports the smooth flow of credit to households and businesses.

citations.quote: Thus, the Discount Window supports the smooth flow of credit to households and businesses.

obligations.action: secure/collateralize discount window advances to the satisfaction of the Reserve Bank
obligations.trigger: receipt of a discount window advance

citations.quote: Discount window advances must be secured by collateral acceptable to the Reserve Bank.
All discount window advances must be collateralized to the satisfaction of the Reserve Bank.

obligations.actor: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System / Reserve Banks
obligations.action: obtain Board of Governors approval, in consultation with the Secretary of the Treasury, for emergency credit programs

citations.quote: Such emergency credit programs must be approved by the Board of Governors, in consultation with the Secretary of the Treasury.

obligations.actor: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
obligations.action: authorize the Reserve Banks to provide credit to institutions that qualify under broad-based eligibility criteria

citations.quote: In unusual and exigent circumstances, the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System may authorize the Reserve Banks to provide credit to institutions that qualify under broad-based eligibility criteria.

obligations.action: limit extending advances to depository institutions
obligations.trigger: depository institution has fallen below minimum capital standards or received a poor supervisory rating from its federal supervisor

citations.quote: Federal Reserve Banks have limitations on extending advances to depository institutions that have fallen below minimum capital standards or have received a poor supervisory rating from its federal supervisor.

obligations.action: pay accrued interest on advances to the lending Reserve Bank
obligations.trigger: at maturity or when repayment of principal on the advance is requested

citations.quote: Accrued interest on advances is due and payable to the lending Reserve Bank at maturity or when repayment of principal on the advance is requested.

obligations.actor: Reserve Bank (as lender of secondary credit)
obligations.action: extend secondary credit to meet backup liquidity needs
obligations.trigger: use is consistent with a timely return to a reliance on market sources of funding or the orderly resolution of a troubled institution

citations.quote: Secondary credit is available to meet backup liquidity needs when its use is consistent with a timely return to a reliance on market sources of funding or the orderly resolution of a troubled institution.

obligations.trigger: can demonstrate a clear pattern of recurring intra-yearly swings in funding needs

citations.quote: Seasonal credit may be available to depository institutions with deposits of $500 million or less that can demonstrate a clear pattern of recurring intra-yearly swings in funding needs.

definitions.definition: Federal Reserve Banks (Reserve Banks) extend credit to banks, credit unions and other depository institutions through ordinary lending programs, collectively referred to as the Discount Window.

citations.quote: Federal Reserve Banks (Reserve Banks) extend credit to banks, credit unions and other depository institutions through ordinary lending programs, collectively referred to as the Discount Window.

definitions.definition: Available to depository institutions in generally sound condition on a short-term basis and at a rate relative to the Federal Open Market Committee's target range of the federal funds rate.

citations.quote: Primary credit is available to depository institutions in generally sound condition on a short-term basis and at a rate relative to the Federal Open Market Committee's target range of the federal funds rate.

definitions.definition: May be available to depository institutions that are not eligible for primary credit; extended on a very short-term basis, typically overnight, at a rate above the primary credit rate.

citations.quote: Secondary credit may be available to depository institutions that are not eligible for primary credit. It is extended on a very short-term basis, typically overnight, at a rate that is above the primary credit rate.

definitions.definition: May be available to depository institutions with deposits of $500 million or less that can demonstrate a clear pattern of recurring intra-yearly swings in funding needs; advances accrue interest at a floating rate consistent with market rates.

citations.quote: Seasonal credit may be available to depository institutions with deposits of $500 million or less that can demonstrate a clear pattern of recurring intra-yearly swings in funding needs.
Advances accrue interest at a floating rate that is consistent with market rates.

definitions.definition: Financial institutions that are considered “depository institutions” under Section 19(b)(1)(A) of the Federal Reserve Act, and that maintain reservable transaction accounts or nonpersonal time deposits (as defined in Regulation D) are eligible to participate in discount window lending programs.

citations.quote: Financial institutions that are considered “depository institutions” under Section 19(b)(1)(A) of the Federal Reserve Act, and that maintain reservable transaction accounts or nonpersonal time deposits (as defined in Regulation D) are eligible to participate in discount window lending programs.

notes: This source is an operational specification of the Fed's own Discount Window (primary/secondary/seasonal credit, collateral, eligibility, emergency credit) and does not itself mention FHLB rules, discount-window stigma, or Call Report/FR 2052a reporting timing/granularity; it is extracted here solely as the Federal Reserve-side operational baseline evidence against which fragmentation/interoperability with FHLB rules, stigma sources, and reporting-timing defects (to be identified from other corpus items) would later be mapped. Per fidelity rule, wording such as 'may be available,' 'have limitations on,' and 'is due and payable' is preserved as-is even though modality is not always phrased as clear shall/must language; classification into must/conditional above reflects best-fit mapping of the text's own phrasing, not harmonization of substance. No content on Acting Comptroller Hsu, Undersecretary McKernan, or reform proposals appears in this source.
